newsitem.title: CHINA: FORECAST - China bank sees 1996 growth at 9.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - China bank sees 1996 growth at 9.8 pct.

text.p: China is within reach of achieving economic growth of 9.8 percent this year, the Financial News on Tuesday quoted Dai Xianglong, head of the People's Bank of China, the central bank, as saying.
China's broad M2 money supply growth could be around 26 percent, down from 26.5 percent in 1995, while foreign exchange reserves could exceed $100 billion, the newspaper quoted Dai as saying.
Last month Dai said gross domestic product should grow by between nine and 10 percent this year, down from 10.2 percent in 1995.
The central bank had set a target for M2 money supply growth in 1996 of 25 percent.
China's tight monetary policies had achieved clear success, the Financial News quoted Dai as saying.
He said retail price inflation could be kept within 6.6 percent, down from 14.8 percent in 1995 and well within the official target for 1996 of 10 percent.
